user.title: Add a pet
user.description: Each pet lives in its own little handheld device, shown by the Hatch at Home pet shelf card. To add another pet later, add Hatch at Home again.

data_description.name: What everyone calls it: on the card, in notifications and to voice assistants. It also names the pet's entities, like button.pip_feed.
data_description.world: Sets the device's look and which creatures can hatch. The egg picks one by surprise.
data_description.dashboard: Optional. Where you'll put the pet shelf card. Tapping one of this pet's notifications opens it, and so does the welcome. Pick one or type a path, like /lovelace/pets.

reconfigure.title: Rename {name} or change its world
reconfigure.description: A new name shows everywhere the pet does; its entity IDs stay the same. A newly laid egg can also be named on the card during its first day. A new world changes the device and which creatures hatch.

reconfigure_hatched.title: Rename {name} or change its world
reconfigure_hatched.description: A new name shows everywhere the pet does; its entity IDs stay the same. A newly laid egg can also be named on the card during its first day. A new world changes the device and which creatures hatch.

data_description.world: {name} stays where it is. Its next egg starts in this world.

error.name_taken: Another pet here already has that name.

abort.no_worlds: No pet worlds are ready yet. Reinstall the integration files and try again.

init.title: What {name} notices
init.description: Pick what {name} notices. Everything is optional, and the house never hurts the pet: it only changes its mood, its scene and what it asks for.

menu_option_descriptions.bedtime: When the pet goes to bed and wakes up
menu_option_descriptions.people: Who's home, the sitter, and privacy
menu_option_descriptions.weather: Rain, sun, indoor temperature and air
menu_option_descriptions.house: Heating, fans, machines, chores and visitors

bedtime.title: {name}'s bedtime
bedtime.description: Bedtime and wake time are targets: the pet may turn in up to an hour either side, and lights out always wins. It sleeps when the bedtime lights are off and the house is quiet.

data_description.bedtime: It gets drowsy 30 minutes before. Switching "Lights out" off again after bedtime costs a little happiness.
data_description.wake_time: It wakes up on its own at this time.
data_description.bedtime_lights: When all of these are off, it's time for bed. Bedroom lights work well. A light left on late doesn't keep the pet up past its own bedtime.
data_description.motion: Indoor motion, occupancy or presence sensors. Movement in the last 10 minutes means the house isn't quiet yet.

people.title: People and privacy
people.description: Who is home decides whether the pet is with you or at the sitter's. The privacy switches decide what dashboards and sensors may show.

data.sitter_settles: The sitter calms a fussy pet
data.memory: Pets may remember what people tell them

data_description.zone: The pet counts the people in this zone. Only people tracked in Home Assistant count.
data_description.away_after: How long the house has to be empty first.
data_description.sitter_settles: On: if the pet was fussing for attention when it left (not a real need), the sitter settles it, so it comes home happy. Off: the fussing waits for you. Real needs, like hunger, always wait.
data_description.privacy: On: an empty house shows the pet napping, never at the sitter's, and the pet never names anyone on sensors. For a wall tablet, also turn on "shared screen" in the card's settings.
data_description.house_words_private: On: news headlines and a house moment's own words are said on the card only, never kept on the pet's sensors (automations still get a headline). Off: they sit on the last-care sensor for a while, like the pet's other moments.
data_description.memory: On: each person may turn memory on for themselves, on their own screen, and this pet keeps their picks and tags (dates and fixed choices, never typed words or names) until they forget them. Off: this pet keeps and says nothing from memory. Off on every pet erases what everyone told their pets.

weather.title: Weather and air
weather.description: The pet sees the weather outside and feels the room's temperature and air. It never gets sick from them.

data_description.rain: An on/off "it's raining" entity, or a rain rate where anything above 0 means rain. This beats the forecast, which only says what's likely.
data_description.weather: A weather entity. Used for sunny, snow and fog, and for rain when there's no rain sensor.
data_description.indoor_temperature: One temperature sensor in the main living space.
data_description.comfort_low: Below this the pet shivers and asks for a blanket. Never when the fireplace is lit.
data_description.comfort_high: Above this the pet sweats and asks for a fan.
data_description.aqi: An air quality index sensor. Above 100 the pet wears a little mask and stays in. Cosmetic only.
data_description.solar: Only if your weather station reports solar radiation in W/m². 300 or more counts as sunny, more precise than the forecast.

room.title: {name}'s room
room.description: Lights, a fireplace, the TV and music change the pet's scene and mood.

data_description.room_lights: Lights in that room, for example the living room. Still on at half brightness or more after bedtime counts as too bright; before bedtime they never do.
data_description.fireplace: Any entity that's on, heating or above 0 when the fire is lit. The pet curls up by it, gets a little happier, and won't ask for a blanket.
data_description.lux: Optional. 100 lx or more after bedtime also counts as too bright.
data_description.tv: Media players that are TVs. On or playing counts as watching.
data_description.music: Speakers and displays. Playing anything that isn't video counts as music.

house.title: The house helps
house.description: When the heating or a fan comes on as the pet asks, the house answers for you. Finished machines, ticked-off chores, robot vacuums and the doorbell give it something to notice.

data.appliance_watts: Counts as off at or below

data_description.heating: A thermostat, switch or toggle that is on when the heating is. A thermostat counts while it is heating (or set to heat and below its target). Pick the one for the pet's room: many homes run the heating when nobody is cold.
data_description.cooling: A fan, thermostat, switch or toggle that is on when the room is being cooled. A thermostat counts while it is cooling or running its fan.
data_description.notice_robot: Every vacuum in the house counts. One added later is noticed once these settings are saved again.
data_description.notice_doorbell: Every doorbell in the house counts. One added later is noticed once these settings are saved again.
data_description.appliances: Machines that finish a cycle. A switch or sensor that reports power, a sensor that says running and finished, or a binary sensor that is on while it runs. When one finishes the pet says so, once.
data_description.appliance_watts: For power readings: at or below this many watts means the machine is not running. A cycle is seen after 10 minutes running, and over after about 3 minutes idle.
data_description.chores: To-do lists. Each item someone ticks off earns the pet a treat (up to 5 a day); it waits if the pet is asleep or away.

sky.title: Moon and sky
sky.description: The moon sensors make the pet's night sky match yours, full moons and all.

data_description.moon_phase: A sensor whose state is the phase, like "full_moon" or "Full Moon".
data_description.moon_illumination: Optional. The lit fraction, 0–1 or a percentage; 97% or more counts as full.
data_description.moon_altitude: Optional. Degrees above the horizon; the moon only counts while it's up.

notifications.title: Where notifications open
notifications.description: Phone notifications go to whoever taps "notify me" on the pet's status screen.

data_description.dashboard: Tapping one of this pet's notifications opens this dashboard. Pick one or type a path, like /lovelace/pets. Empty opens the app as it was.

error.comfort_range: "Too cold below" must be lower than "Too warm above".
error.same_times: Bedtime and wake time can't be the same, or the pet would never sleep.
error.fireplace_temperature: Pick the fireplace's switch, power sensor or climate entity. A temperature sensor is always above 0, so the fire would always look lit.

no_pet.message: No loaded virtual pet matches that pet or config entry.

no_reaction.message: A Custom house moment needs a reaction: hop, cheer, cozy, dance or startle.

wrong_guess.message: "{guess}" isn't a guess in that game; try {guesses}.

not_signed_in.message: Only someone signed in can turn their own pet notifications on or off.

shell_locked.message: The {finish} shell opens once the pet is a {stage}.

fast_forward.name: Fast forward (testing)
fast_forward.description: Debug tool: lives through the given number of hours right now, at normal rates. Calls left unanswered in that time count as care misses.

config_entry_id.name: Pet
config_entry_id.description: Which pet. Leave empty for all pets.

notify_me.name: Notify me
notify_me.description: Turns this pet's phone notifications on or off for you, the user calling it. They go to your phones through the Home Assistant app: calls, sickness, hatching, growing up, traits, the season's first snow and frost, and new eggs.

enabled.name: Enabled
enabled.description: On to get notifications, off to stop.

visit.name: Visit
visit.description: Tells the pet that you, the user calling it, looked in. The card calls it when you open it: the first visit of the day counts toward your bond with the pet, and an afternoon visit grants a "come say hi" wish. Counted at most hourly. It answers with anything the pet saved to tell only you.

my_day.name: My day
my_day.description: Lets the pet notice your day, or stops it, for you, the user calling it: steps, stairs, a bike ride or a run, and a good night's sleep, from the phones you signed in to the Home Assistant app with. It only ever says something when a day stands out for the better, and only to you. The closer your bond, the more it notices.

enabled.name: Enabled
enabled.description: On to let it notice your day, off to stop.

set_shell.name: Set shell
set_shell.description: Dresses the pet's device in a shell finish, or back in its world's own. The glitter, glow, smoke, sunset, constellation and stars shells open once the pet is a teen. Home Assistant's history records this action and who ran it; on the card, picking a shell is not recorded.

finish.name: Finish
finish.description: The finish's key, such as stripes, hearts or camo. Leave it out for the world's own.

play_game.name: Play a game
play_game.description: One round of a game the card's play button starts. Five rounds make a game. Left or right: the pet hides left or right and you guess; the first guess starts a game; three right guesses win. Higher or lower: call once without a guess to start and see the first number (1-9), then guess whether the next is higher or lower; three right guesses win. Berry dig: call once without a guess to start; each round a leaf pile hides 6 berries and 2 bees. Dig turns one leaf (a berry goes in the basket, a bee scares the basket off and ends the round); keep banks the basket and ends the round. 5 berries banked win.

guess.name: Guess
guess.description: Left or right; lower or higher; keep or dig. Leave it out to start a game.

end.name: End
end.description: End the game in progress instead of playing a round: no reward, no penalty, nothing logged. Does nothing if there is none, or it is another game. A berry dig that has started is put aside instead for whoever ends it (one shared slot for calls with no person, such as automations), and their next dig carries on from it.

shared.name: Shared screen
shared.description: Set by the card on a shared screen: a berry dig put aside there is the household's, not the signed-in user's.

hop.name: Hop of the Day
hop.description: Hop of the Day, the pet's daily board game. The board action returns today's board for the pet: the same on every screen all day, built once and kept until midnight, and refused (result egg, asleep, away or too_tired) when the pet could not play a game now. The settle action sends the moves of a board played to the nest; the server replays them and pays the day's first win, and one find for the day's first tidy win. A later settle the same day answers ok with already true. Other results: illegal, not_won, too_long, board_changed (load today's board), egg, asleep or away.

action.name: Action
action.description: board: return today's board. settle: replay and pay a board played to the nest.

id.name: Board
id.description: Settle: the id of the board that was played, from the board action's reply.

moves.name: Moves
moves.description: Settle: the moves from the start, one letter per move: the cell stepped on, a to x in reading order.

shared.name: Shared screen
shared.description: Set by the card on a shared screen. Settle only.

share_news.name: Share news
share_news.description: Tells the pet a bit of news, and it says it in its speech bubble on the card ('did you hear? ...'). Cosmetic only: no stat changes. Dropped while the pet is asleep, away or still an egg, and at most one bit of news shows every 30 minutes per pet.

entity_id.name: Pet
entity_id.description: Any entity of the pet. Pick several for several pets.

headline.name: Headline
headline.description: What the pet says. Extra spaces are tidied away and anything past 60 characters is cut at a word.

topic.name: Topic
topic.description: Optional short label, such as the feed's name (up to 20 characters).

react.name: House moment
react.description: Something in the house happened, and the pet reacts with a line of its own (the "house moment" blueprint calls this). Cosmetic only: no stat changes, nothing saved, no notification. Dropped while the pet is asleep, away or still an egg; each kind of thing shows at most once every 10 minutes.

entity_id.name: Pet
entity_id.description: Any entity of the pet. Pick several for several pets.

category.name: What it is
category.description: The kind of thing that changed. It picks the pet's line, reaction and effect, and which changes count.

source.name: Entity
source.description: The entity that changed. Read to check the change and to step aside for entities the pet's own house settings already watch; never kept.

from_state.name: From state
from_state.description: The state it changed from. Leave out, with To state, to always count.

held.name: Held for
held.description: Seconds the old state held (a washer must have run a while to be done).

match.name: State that counts
match.description: Custom only: the state that counts, such as "finished". Empty: any change.

reaction.name: Reaction
reaction.description: Custom only: how the pet reacts.

text.name: Words
text.description: Custom only, optional: what the pet says, up to 40 characters. Empty: the reaction's own line.

missing_entities.title: {pet} is listening for entities that are gone

confirm.title: {pet} is listening for entities that are gone
confirm.description:
{pet}'s settings mention entities that no longer exist in Home Assistant: {entities}.

Submit to forget them: {pet} stops listening for them, and nothing else in its settings changes. To use new entities instead, close this and open Settings → Devices & services → Hatch at Home → the gear next to {pet}, then {topics}.

abort.entry_gone: This pet has been removed, so there is nothing to forget.

world_not_ready.title: {pet}'s world has no creatures yet
world_not_ready.description: {pet} lives in {world}, but none of that world's creatures are installed and ready, so its egg can't hatch. It stays an egg, safe and frozen in place, until they are. Reinstall or update the integration's files; if this keeps happening, please report it.

save_damaged.title: {pet}'s save file was damaged
save_damaged.description: Part of {pet}'s save file couldn't be read. {pet} kept its name, family, journal, memories and bonds where they could be read, and started the rest fresh. The file as it was is kept as `.storage/{backup}`. To go back to it: stop Home Assistant, fix the file, rename it to `.storage/virtual_pet.{entry_id}`, and start Home Assistant again.

save_damaged_egg.title: {pet}'s save file was damaged
save_damaged_egg.description: {pet}'s save file couldn't be read at all, so {pet} started again as an egg. The file as it was is kept as `.storage/{backup}` (Home Assistant adds `.corrupt` and the time to the name of a file it can't read). To go back to it: stop Home Assistant, fix the file, rename it to `.storage/virtual_pet.{entry_id}`, and start Home Assistant again.

save_damaged_missing.title: {pet}'s save file was damaged
save_damaged_missing.description: {pet}'s save file is missing, so {pet} started again as an egg. No copy of the old file was left to restore.

people_damaged.title: The pets' memories of people were damaged
people_damaged.description: The file where the pets keep what they know about each person (birthdays, answers, settings) couldn't be read, so they start fresh with everyone. Your pets and your bonds with them are fine. The file as it was is kept as `.storage/{backup}`. To go back to it: stop Home Assistant, fix the file, rename it to `.storage/virtual_pet.people`, and start Home Assistant again.
